subject: Axios Pro Rata: Claude crushes it

Plus, the *other* big AI deal | Thursday, November 19, 2026
 
View in browser
 
Axios Pro Rata
By Dan Primack · Nov 19, 2026

𖥂 Our third annual Axios Future of Defense Summit kicks off today at 1:45pm ET in Washington, D.C.

  • Guests include Boeing Defense CEO Steve Parker, In-Q-Tel CEO Steve Bowsher, Washington Harbour Partners CEO Mina Faltas, XYZ Venture Capital managing partner Ross Fubini, Mach Industries CEO Ethan Thornton, Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.) and Sen. Joni Ernst (R-Iowa).
  • Watch the livestream
Share today’s Axios Pro Rata
 
 
Top of the Morning
 

Photo illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Photo: Ben Hider/Getty Images
 

Wall Street isn't sweating existential threats to humanity. That's a tomorrow problem. Today there's money to make.

Driving the news: Anthropic last night raised $81.35 billion in its IPO, after pricing 980 million shares at $83 per share. It had planned to sell 825 million shares at $70-$78 per share.

  • This is expected to be the largest IPO ever, topping SpaceX, assuming that underwriters exercise their greenshoes. And that's not even including a concurrent $26 billion private placement.
  • Anthropic's initial market value would be nearly $1.1 trillion, with a fully diluted value of around $1.5 trillion. But all of that will be moot once shares begin trading, with a pop all but guaranteed.

ROI: Anthropic was valued at $965 billion after its most recent private round, led by Dragoneer, Coatue, Sequoia Capital, Greenoaks, and Altimeter.

  • It first raised venture money in early 2021 at a $461 million post-money valuation led by Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn.
  • Sam Bankman-Fried (yes, that one) led the Series B round one year later at a $3 billion post-money valuation. In 2023, Anthropic was valued at $4.6 billion after a Series C round led by Spark Capital, Salesforce Ventures, Zoom Ventures, and Alphabet.

The big picture: It's too early to know if this is just FOMO or a sincere belief that AI trade tumult is really in the rearview.

  • But it's nonetheless a remarkable achievement. The Trump administration in March tried to kneecap Anthropic by broadly designating it a "supply chain risk," but courts later limited the impact.
  • Two months ago, Anthropic's own CEO wrote about "pacing the frontier." OpenAI pushed its own IPO into 2027 and lots of folks fretted that the Claude maker would follow suit.
  • Then came the management mess at Nvidia, one of Anthropic's major investors and strategic partners.

Brief bull case: Demand is to infinity and beyond. Anthropic beat its top rival to the public markets and now has tons of cash to pay for compute and build up its application layer via acquisition. It also has a glide path to the indices, and had a roadshow chart claiming that the company is learning to produce intelligence with less compute.

Brief bear case: Enterprise's eyes might have been bigger than their stomachs for AI spend, particularly with open-source alternatives, and the nearly $900 billion in compute obligations remain onerous. Plus, its top rival gets to continue operating as a private company — without the public market's glare or reporting obligations.

The bottom line: This is one IPO for one company, but the tech ecosystem ripples are sure to be wide.

  • It's sure to mint thousands of new millionaires, many of whom will go on to become angel investors. Eligible employees can sell up to 10% of vested shares on Day 1.
  • It also should lead to record distributions for a huge swath of VC funds — many of which also were in SpaceX — thus keeping institutional investors in the LP game.
  • In short, the startup flywheel keeps spinning.
 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios
 

Palo Alto Networks (Nasdaq: PANW) agreed to acquire Applied Compute, a developer of open-source AI models for enterprises, for $4.5 billion in stock.

Why it's the BFD: Companies want to adopt AI agents but are terrified of what they might do if left to their own devices. Palo Alto is betting that customized open-weight models are a safety solve, so long as cybersecurity is baked in from the jump.

ROI: Applied Compute had raised $510 million in VC funding since being founded just last year, including $350 million in September at a $3.25 billion valuation (the round was publicly announced earlier this month).

  • Backers include Elad Gil, Kleiner Perkins, Lux Capital, Hanabi Capital, Nvidia, Blackstone, Shopify Ventures, HubSpot Ventures, Diffusion, Definition, Timeless, Layer Global, Neo, Abstract, Nova, Quantum Light, First Harmonic, and Swish.

The bottom line: "Cybersecurity fears rose following a string of technology outages across US companies and government agencies in the span of a week... AI is adding to the risk by accelerating the discovery of software vulnerabilities and shrinking the time companies have to respond." — Bloomberg
 
 
Venture Capital Deals
 

🚑 Boltz, a London-based AI drug discovery startup, raised $110m in Series A funding. Bessemer Venture Partners led, joined by a16z, Amplify Partners, Zetta Venture Partners, and Obvious Ventures. axios.link/4f2Of8z

• BrightAI, a Palo Alto, Calif.-based infrastructure monitoring startup, raised $97m. Smith Point Capital led, joined by Cobalt Capital, Marlinspike Partners, Zero Infinity Partners, GE Vernova, Khosla Ventures, Inspired Capital, and Upfront Ventures. axios.link/4j3wO92

🚑 Ansa Biotechnologies, an Emeryville, Calif.-based DNA synthesis startup, raised $71.5m in Series C funding. Blue Water Life Science Advisors led, joined by Illumina Ventures, BEVC, Lightscape Partners, Agent Capital and insiders Cerberus Ventures, Fall Line Capital, Dauntless Ventures and Altitude Life Science Ventures. axios.link/4iXwwQN

• Pulley, a permitting platform for developers, raised $41m in Series B funding, per Axios Pro. Jump Capital led, joined by Catalyst Investors, CRV, Susa Ventures, South Park Commons, and Suffolk Technologies. axios.link/3V5sspE

• Humyn Labs, an SF-based physical AI research startup, raised $26m in Series A equity funding. Accel led, joined by Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, and Jump Trading. It also secured $21m in debt led by Lighthouse Canton with participation from Trifecta Capital. axios.link/3UY7Xew

• StepSecurity, a software supply chain security platform, raised $20m in Series A funding, per Axios Pro. Elephant led, joined by insiders Runtime Ventures, Inner Loop Capital, and SaaS Ventures. axios.link/4C9i7d5

• Nodal Networks, an LA-based shipping hub intelligence startup, raised $11.3m in seed funding, per Axios Pro. Eniac Ventures led, joined by NewRoad Capital Partners and returning investors Riot Ventures, Trail Mix Ventures, and Liquid 2 Ventures. axios.link/4t7jjcO

⚡️ Darcy Geothermal, a New Brighton, Minn.-based geothermal heating and cooling provider, raised $15m in Series B funding led by Aligned Climate Capital and Büetigen. axios.link/48pw6Ov

• Unsiloed AI, an SF-based provider of document-processing software, raised $7.5m in seed funding. Felicis led, joined by YC, Orange Collective, and Uncorrelated Ventures. axios.link/4j2n0Me

• EachLabs, a generative media platform for businesses, raised $7m in seed funding. Revo Capital led, joined by ERBD. axios.link/4zwbvDb

🚑 Tesorai, a San Diego-based "searchable knowledge layer for life sciences," raised $5.3m in seed funding from Perplexity Fund, IQT, South Central Ventures, New Stack Ventures, NextGen Venture Partners, f7 Ventures, VitalStage Ventures, and ZAKA. axios.link/4j3UlGT

• LATO, a market research startup, raised $4.7m in seed funding. Air Street Capital and Axiom Partners led, joined by YC, Montis VC, and Inception Fund. axios.link/4thaD3S

🌎 Provectus Algae, an Australian developer of algae-based products, raised US$4.3m in Series A extension funding from At One Ventures and Queensland Investment Corp. axios.link/493JkR1

• Wilgot, a Stockholm-based brand recommendation for agents, raised $3m in seed funding led by Industrifonden. axios.link/4t5Xquu
 
 
Private Equity Deals
 

• Advent International is in exclusive talks to buy Singaporean corporate services provider Boardroom for upwards of US$775m from 65 Equity Partners and Tower Capital Asia, per Bloomberg. axios.link/48o1g8V

• Apis Partners Group acquired a minority stake in Alchemy Underwriting, a London-based specialist insurance underwriter. axios.link/48tDAA0

🚑 ICG invested in Chronos Dental, a French dental laboratory group. axios.link/4filBA9

• Kingswood Capital Management agreed to buy the industrial segment of Textron (NYSE: TXT) for $1.2b. axios.link/4t86a3m

⚡ KKR bought a minority stake in Gentari's renewables unit in India. axios.link/48vPeu4

🚑 LGI Healthcare Solutions, backed by Investissement Québec and Novacap Management, acquired QHR Technologies, a Canadian provider of electronic medical records software. axios.link/48uBTCl

⚾ Partners Group agreed to acquire a stake in Rawlings Sporting Goods at a reported $2b enterprise value, while existing backers Major League Baseball and Seidler Equity Partners retain "meaningful ownership." axios.link/48tbyEO

⚡ Promera, backed by Angeles Equity Partners, acquired B&G Energy, an Ireland-based electrical contractor. axios.link/4zZUJgK

• Regiment Security Partners, a Yonkers, N.Y.-based provider of contracted security services, raised funding from Tecum Capital Partners, Capital Alignment Partners, Expedition Capital Partners, and LO3 Capital. axios.link/498bfPL

• Ridgemont Equity Partners invested in Strategic Resource Management, an advisory for financial institutions. axios.link/4ChJdyU

• Vitruvian Partners invested in IGEL, a German adaptive security endpoint platform backed by TA Associates, at a valuation north of $1b. axios.link/4jpOdZN
 
 
Public Offerings
 

🚑 Laprophan, a Moroccan drugmaker, raised around $223m in a Casablanca IPO. axios.link/4CdwbCe
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

• PDI Partners, backed by Insight Partners and other PE firms, sold Azpiral (digital engagement systems) and htec (retail tech), to Henderson Technology. axios.link/4C9J8Nr

🌎 Reploid, an Austrian insect ag company, agreed to acquire Chapul Farms, a McMinnville, Ore.-based insect ag company, for about $12m. Chapul investors include Nexus PMG and Mark Cuban Cos. axios.link/4A6HpqI
 
 
More M&A
 

• Accor (Paris: ACCP) agreed to buy out the minority shareholders in Ennismore, a London-based lifestyle hospitality company, for around €1.6b. axios.link/4zuVrS4

🚑 Disco Pharmaceuticals, a VC-backed German biotech initially focused on lung and colorectal cancers, signed a strategic collaboration and option-to-license agreement with AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) that includes $40m upfront and up to $2.5b in earnouts. Disco backers include AbbVie Ventures. axios.link/4iXvF2x
 
 
It's Personnel
 

• Loren Schlachet is stepping down as a managing partner at The Riverside Co., which he joined 27 years ago, to launch a new PE firm focused on micro-cap opportunities. axios.link/48ooFqK

🌎 Nate Sweet joined OpenAI as its clean energy lead. Sweet was previously senior director for corporate development and M&A at Primergy. axios.link/3UZs3Fe
 
 
Final Numbers
